transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

A wash-pump or heating fault is less likely unless the machine is quiet during washing or everything is coming out cold. 1. Switch the dishwasher off and unplug it. Pull out the lower basket, twist/lift out the filter in the base, and rinse it thoroughly under the tap. Clear away any food debris from its housing with a cloth. This stops debris being drawn back into the wash water. 2. Check both spray arms turn freely by hand. Remove them if they unclip easily, rinse them, and clear their small jet holes with a wooden cocktail stick — not a drill or metal tool. A blocked hole or a tall item stopping an arm will leave food residue behind. 3. Check the next load is not blocking either arm: tall trays, pan handles and long utensils are common culprits. Use a normal or intensive programme rather than a quick cycle for dried-on food. If the filter and arms are clean but it still leaves grit everywhere, listen during the wash: a proper wash should sound like steady sloshing/spraying. Silence or a continuous hum without spray points more towards the circulation system and is an engineer job.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok will try that. filter was full of food n grease. upper spray arm is stiff when i turn it by hand, lower one spins fine. should i do anything else?

Yes — the upper arm is the next thing to deal with. 1. Switch the dishwasher off and unplug it. Remove the upper spray arm only if it releases in the normal way, then rinse it through under the tap. Clear each small jet hole with a wooden cocktail stick; food particles or scale can stop it rotating.
2. Check it is not cracked, split, loose or rubbing against the upper basket when refitted. It should turn freely by hand without catching.
3. Run one normal or intensive wash afterwards, with nothing tall or loose that can obstruct either arm. If the upper arm frees up after cleaning, it was most likely a blockage rather than a failed pump. If it remains stiff despite clear holes and no obstruction, or is cracked/loose, the upper spray arm or its mounting is the likely faulty component; don’t order anything until that check suggests it.
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok did the upper arm, a few holes were blocked with seeds n limescale, cleared them w a cocktail stick. what programme shud i run? i was using the quick 30 min one

Run a Normal/Daily programme, or Intensive if the load has dried-on food. For prevention, rinse the filter every week or two and check the spray-arm holes occasionally, especially if limescale builds up. If the next normal wash comes out clean, it is resolved. If it is still poor, tell me whether it is worse on the top rack or throughout the machine.
